solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two short cuts to good health

parts.note: no letters of its own: it says the next piece is used twice

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its tail, so each word loses its final letter

parts.note: a chine is a butcher's cut of meat along the backbone

explanation.surface: Someone recommends trimming a couple of things for the sake of their wellbeing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two chines, each docked of its last letter, give CHIN-CHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an old-fashioned drinking toast, said when raising glasses, exactly like wishing someone well.

clue.text: Data introduced to win over meeting

indicators.note: something introduced to another is put inside it

parts.note: to convert someone is to win them over to your side
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Facts are brought in to persuade the attendees of a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting' looks like a noun, a gathering, but it is the adjective: coming together.
explanation.definitionFit: Convergent lines or ideas come together at a point, so they are meeting.

clue.text: Sort of mine not left by American force

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a limpet mine is one clamped to a ship's hull
L is the abbreviation for left
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A kind of explosive was not planted by the US military.
explanation.walkthrough: A limpet mine is one clamped magnetically to a ship's hull; 'force' looks like the military but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving momentum or energy that pushes something onward.

clue.text: Cold serving of beer beside a climbing plant

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: a pint is the standard British measure of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chilled beer served next to a creeper growing up a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing plant' reads as one phrase, but climbing is the reversal signal and plant alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a herb of the mint family whose scent attracts cats.

clue.text: Speak with vet before examining body

indicators.note: before puts the piece that follows it at the front

parts.note: to vet something is to check it over
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Talk to the veterinarian before examining an animal's carcass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' and 'body' suggest an animal doctor and a corpse; 'body' is part of the definition, an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspectorate is an official organisation of inspectors, whose job is checking and reviewing standards.

clue.text: A fake king's in retreat

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one item being in another means it sits inside the other's letters

parts.note: a sham is a fake
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An impostor monarch has gone into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like the container signal for backing away, but it is the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious hermitage, a place people go for spiritual withdrawal from the world.

clue.text: Chess or alternative involving unknown lighter pieces

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside
an alternative version of the letters is a different arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: Chess or some other game with unfamiliar, less heavy playing pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' suggests chessmen, but here it means pieces of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively, light-hearted musical movement, so scherzos are light pieces of music.

clue.text: Take over from priest always twirling robes

indicators.note: to robe something is to clothe it, wrapping around it
twirling means spinning round, so the word is turned back on itself

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A cleric replaced by a colleague who forever spins around in vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's favourite priest, three letters from the Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a sentry or worker is to take their place so they can rest.

clue.text: Tom's cries sounded deliberate

indicators.note: sounded means as heard, so we go by pronunciation

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, whose cries are mews

explanation.surface: Someone's cries came out sounding intentional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb: to think something over.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or think something over, the verb sense of deliberate.

clue.text: Taking on family over claims it openly admits

indicators.note: in an across clue, over means turned back to front
the phrase admits the answer, holding it within its run of letters

parts.note: the letters running across the end of claims, all of it, and the start of openly

explanation.surface: A statement that someone openly concedes hiring their relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, the run MSITOPEN becomes NEPOTISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism toward relatives, especially giving them jobs, which is hiring one's own kin.

clue.text: Benefits after wife gives birth

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the next one

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
helps as a verb: benefits

explanation.surface: A mother receives state benefits once she has had her baby.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelp is to produce young, used of dogs and other animals delivering a litter.

clue.text: First photo's a sprinter, given too much too soon

parts.note: a first photo is shot one, and the apostrophe s stays
Usain Bolt, the Jamaican Olympic sprinter

explanation.surface: An early snapshot of a runner who burnt out quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given too much' reads as a passive, but it is active: having given everything too early.
explanation.definitionFit: Having shot one's bolt means having used up all one's effort or resources prematurely, like an archer firing early.

clue.text: Worry as steed might bolt a lot

parts.note: worry as in gnaw or bother: what's eating you?
as means in the manner of
a steed is a horse

explanation.surface: A rider frets that their horse may suddenly run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' and 'steed' paint a runaway horse, but bolt here means wolf down food; 'might' just rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt food is to gulp it hungrily, so bolting a great deal is the idiom for having a huge appetite.

clue.text: An area of sci-fi advertisers rate

parts.note: people who hype products, promoters
rate as in speed

explanation.surface: Science-fiction territory that marketers rank highly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' looks like a verb, as in judge, but it is a noun: speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperspace is the imagined realm beyond normal space through which fictional starships travel faster than light.

clue.text: My turn to keep quiet

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
sh is the noise telling someone to keep quiet

explanation.surface: A player says it is their go and they must stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, as in 'My, how you've grown' or 'Gosh, how you've grown'.

clue.text: Writers' articles still being reported

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so we go by how the word is heard

parts.note: still means not moving, motionless

explanation.surface: Pieces by authors are still being covered in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writers' looks like authors but means pens and pencils, things that write.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery covers pens, paper and other writing materials, the items used for writing.

clue.text: Tissue produced by soldier, upset during elegy

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: an elegy is a lament for the dead

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read upward

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier cried into a tissue during a funeral song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tissue' suggests a handkerchief at a funeral but it means body tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of tough fibrous tissue joining bones together.

clue.text: Table item about protective fabric before lunch?

definitions.text: Table item about protective fabric before lunch?

parts.note: surface reading: something on the table concerning a cloth that protects
setter's reading: a ring sitting around the folded cloth that guards clothes, until the meal begins and it is pulled out

explanation.surface: A query about some dining accessory and the cloth it relates to.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin ring is a band holding a rolled table napkin at each place setting until the diner uses it.

clue.text: Wrap up season below Wolves?

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the first piece underneath the second

parts.note: wolves hunt in a pack; the question mark flags the example
to season wood or wine is to age it

explanation.surface: Finish off a football season with Wolves near the bottom of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club; here the word means the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To package something is to wrap it up in a parcel for sending.

clue.text: Instrument's top broke, not every other part

indicators.note: dropping every other part leaves only alternating letters

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A musical instrument's upper section has broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument heard in orchestras.

clue.text: Singer able to fly flags

definitions.meaning: second meaning: strings of little decorative flags

explanation.surface: A performer is capable of flying the colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Able to fly flags' reads as one phrase; split it after fly and both halves define.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunting is a finch-like songbird, and also the strings of small flags hung up for celebrations.

clue.text: Journalist's left skewered by a horned beast

indicators.note: has left means gone away, so those letters drop out

parts.note: to skewer is to run through with a spike
ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reporter was gored by a horned animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is 'has', so the journalist has left the word that follows; 'by' just places the A after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, the males of which carry long lyre-shaped horns.

clue.text: Inmates' chests whipped as punishments

indicators.note: whipped as in beaten up like cream, so the letters are thrashed into a new order

parts.note: every letter of both words, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Prisoners were flogged across the torso as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped' fits the flogging picture so neatly that it hides its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastisements are severe rebukes or beatings given as penalties for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Substitute seen putting feet up

indicators.note: putting something up in a down clue lifts the letters so they read from the bottom
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an animal's feet are its paws

explanation.surface: A replacement player is spotted resting on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, the same as to substitute.

clue.text: Sly person beginning to win artist's support

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its first letter
an easel holds up a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: A cunning schemer starts to win over a painter's backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a weasel means they are crafty, devious and untrustworthy, after the animal's reputation.

clue.text: One painting over wild animals' shelters

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it safely inside
wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An artwork depicts wild creatures' dens.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket. 'One' joins the definition: a single painting, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa is a single, world-famous portrait, hanging in the Louvre.

clue.text: Moderately attractive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fairly, as in fairly good
second meaning: good-looking in a delicate way

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one modest compliment, but the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adverb meaning fairly or rather, and as an adjective meaning nice to look at.

clue.text: Smother last bit of strudel in rum

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other's letters

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or peculiar

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: drench the end of the pastry in spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the drink, but it is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle or smother someone is to kill them by stopping their breathing.
